text.p: Dutch food and drinks group BolsWessanen on Tuesday denied Dutch newspaper reports that it was the target of a bid from British food concern Grand Metropolitan Plc.
"With regards to a possible takeover, the management of BolsWessanen has no single indication that this rumour is true," A BolsWessanen spokeswoman said.
BolsWessanen shares were up 6.00 percent to 31.80 guilders by 0925 GMT on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange.
Dutch daily "Het Financieele Dagblad" reported on Tuesday that Grand Metropolitan wanted to pay around 36 guilders per share for BolsWessanen, valuing the group at around three billion guilders.

The paper said the two companies had already devoted more than a week of discussions to what it said was the last stumbling block in the way of a deal, the position of BolsWessanen senior management after a takeover.
Rumours of a takeover by GrandMet surfaced at the end of October, with both groups playing down the speculation at the time.
BolsWessanen has also been linked recently with several potential Dutch suitors, including CSM and trading group Hagemeyer.
